question: Under Hawaii's CDL program, a Class A license covers which type of vehicle?
choice_a: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_b: Any combination of vehicles with a gross combination weight rating (GCWR) of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the towed vehicle(s) exceeds 10,000 pounds
choice_c: Any single vehicle with a GVWR less than 26,001 pounds
choice_d: Any vehicle designed to carry fewer than 16 passengers
explanation: The manual defines Class A Combination Vehicles as any combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 or more pounds, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is more than 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: How does the manual define a Class B vehicle?
choice_a: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR
choice_b: Any combination vehicle with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_c: Any vehicle used exclusively to haul hazardous materials
choice_d: Any vehicle designed to carry 16 or more passengers only
explanation: Class B Heavy Straight Vehicles are any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 or more pounds, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not exceeding 10,000 pounds GVWR; this class includes straight trucks and large buses.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR under 26,001 pounds is included in Hawaii's CDL program as a Class C vehicle only if it meets which condition?
choice_a: It is painted a specific commercial color
choice_b: It is designed to carry 16 or more passengers (including the driver) or is used to transport placarded hazardous materials
choice_c: It is owned by a government agency
choice_d: It was manufactured after 2010
explanation: Vehicles under 26,001 pounds GVWR fall in Class C only if they are designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or are used to transport hazardous materials requiring placards (or select agents/toxins).
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: According to the manual, which of the following requires a CDL?
choice_a: A single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_b: A personal pickup truck used only for commuting
choice_c: Any vehicle registered to a business
choice_d: A trailer weighing less than 5,000 pounds towed by a personal car
explanation: The manual lists a single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more as one of the categories requiring a CDL, along with certain combination vehicles, passenger-carrying vehicles, and hazmat-placarded vehicles.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Who Needs a CDL

question: Which two groups of drivers does the manual say do NOT need a CDL?
choice_a: School bus drivers and taxi drivers
choice_b: Active duty military (including National Guard) operating military vehicles, and federal/state/county firefighters and police operating authorized emergency vehicles
choice_c: Farmers and delivery drivers
choice_d: Tow truck operators and rideshare drivers
explanation: The manual states that active duty military (including National Guard) with military licenses operating military vehicles, and federal, state, and county firefighters and police operating authorized emergency vehicles, do not need a CDL.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Exemptions

question: A driver who wants to haul materials requiring placards under 49 CFR Part 172, Subpart F must obtain which endorsement, and pass what additional federal check?
choice_a: The N endorsement, with no additional check
choice_b: The H (hazardous materials) endorsement, plus a TSA background check including criminal, immigration, and FBI records
choice_c: The T endorsement, with a vision test only
choice_d: The P endorsement, with a state driving record review only
explanation: Drivers hauling placarded hazardous materials must add the H endorsement and pass a special written exam; the TSA and USDOT also require a background check including criminal, immigration, and FBI records for hazmat-certified drivers.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements

question: The Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement applies to a tank with what minimum capacity?
choice_a: An individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more
choice_b: An individual rated capacity of more than 500 gallons only
choice_c: Any tank regardless of size
choice_d: An aggregate rated capacity of exactly 119 gallons
explanation: The N endorsement is required for a CMV designed to transport liquid or gaseous materials in a tank or tanks with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements

question: A driver wishing to drive a vehicle with a design capacity to carry 16 or more people, including the driver, must add which endorsement?
choice_a: The S (school bus) endorsement only
choice_b: The P (passenger) endorsement
choice_c: The N (tank vehicle) endorsement
choice_d: No endorsement is required
explanation: The manual states that drivers who wish to drive a vehicle with a design capacity to carry 16 or more people, including the driver, must add a passenger (P) endorsement and pass a special knowledge examination plus a skills test in a passenger vehicle.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements

question: What must a driver pass to add a School Bus (S) endorsement to a CDL or CLP?
choice_a: Only a vision test
choice_b: A special knowledge examination on safety considerations when transporting passengers in a school bus, and skills tests in a school bus
choice_c: A background check only, with no knowledge exam
choice_d: A doubles/triples knowledge test
explanation: Drivers wishing to drive a school bus must add an S endorsement and must pass a special knowledge examination on safety considerations for transporting passengers in a school bus, plus skills tests in a school bus.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements

question: Which endorsement is required for drivers who want to pull double or triple trailers?
choice_a: The T (Double and Triple Trailers) endorsement
choice_b: The X endorsement
choice_c: The S endorsement
choice_d: The N endorsement
explanation: The manual states that Class A drivers who wish to pull double or triple trailers must add the T endorsement, which requires passing a special knowledge examination on the problems associated with pulling multiple trailers.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements

question: What does the X endorsement represent?
choice_a: A restriction preventing passenger transport
choice_b: A combination endorsement for drivers of tank vehicles who haul hazardous materials or waste requiring placards, showing they passed both the tank vehicle and hazardous materials exams
choice_c: An endorsement solely for double and triple trailers
choice_d: A medical variance indicator
explanation: The X endorsement is a Combination Hazardous Materials and Tank Vehicle endorsement, required for drivers of tank vehicles hauling hazmat or waste in amounts requiring placards, and it shows they passed the special knowledge exams for both tank vehicles and hazardous materials.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements

question: Which endorsements may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
choice_a: H, T, and X only
choice_b: Only the H endorsement
choice_c: Passenger (P), School bus (S), and Tank vehicle (N)
choice_d: All six endorsements
explanation: The manual specifies that the only endorsements that may be added to a CLP are Passenger (P), School bus (S), and Tank vehicle (N).
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements

question: What does restriction code E mean on a Hawaii CDL?
choice_a: No air brake equipped CMV
choice_b: No manual transmission CMV
choice_c: No passengers in CMV bus
choice_d: No cargo in CMV tank vehicle
explanation: If an applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle with an automatic transmission, the state must indicate restriction code E, meaning the person is restricted from operating a CMV equipped with a manual transmission.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Restrictions

question: A CLP holder who is issued a Passenger (P) or School Bus (S) endorsement must also carry which restriction code?
choice_a: Code X - no cargo in a CMV tank vehicle
choice_b: Code P - no passengers in a CMV bus
choice_c: Code L - no air brakes
choice_d: Code K - intrastate only
explanation: The manual notes that if a CLP is issued with a Passenger (P) or School Bus (S) endorsement, it must also contain a P restriction prohibiting the CLP holder from carrying passengers in a CMV bus, other than certain auditors, examiners, trainees, and the accompanying CDL holder.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Restrictions

question: A CLP holder issued a Tank vehicle (N) endorsement must also carry which restriction code, and what does it mean?
choice_a: Code X, meaning the CLP holder may only operate an empty, purged tank vehicle and is prohibited from carrying cargo in a CMV tank vehicle
choice_b: Code M, meaning no Class A passenger vehicle
choice_c: Code Z, meaning no full air brake equipped CMV
choice_d: Code V, meaning a medical variance exists
explanation: If a CLP is issued with an N endorsement, it must also carry restriction X, meaning the holder may only operate an empty tank vehicle and is prohibited from operating any tank vehicle that previously held hazardous materials and has not been purged.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Restrictions

question: To obtain a Hawaii Commercial Learner's Permit, an applicant must meet several requirements. Which of the following is one of them?
choice_a: Be domiciled in Hawaii and pass a vision test
choice_b: Own a commercial vehicle
choice_c: Have at least five years of driving experience
choice_d: Hold a college degree
explanation: Among the CLP requirements listed, an applicant must be domiciled in Hawaii, fill out an application (DOT 4-764), and pass a vision test, along with a knowledge test for the intended class and endorsements.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, CLP Requirements

question: How long is a Hawaii Commercial Learner's Permit valid, and how soon after obtaining it may a holder take the practical (skills) test?
choice_a: Valid for 90 days; may test immediately
choice_b: Valid for 180 days, renewable once for another 180 days without retaking the knowledge tests; holder must wait at least 14 days before taking the practical test
choice_c: Valid for one year with no waiting period
choice_d: Valid for 30 days, non-renewable
explanation: The manual states the CLP is valid for 180 days and can be renewed once for another 180 days without retaking the knowledge tests, and that the holder must wait at least 14 days after obtaining the permit before taking the practical test.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, How Long is a CLP Valid?

question: Under the Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) regulations, what must a CDL applicant do before taking the Class A or Class B CDL skills test, the S or P skills test, or the H knowledge test?
choice_a: Nothing additional; ELDT is optional
choice_b: Complete training from a provider listed on FMCSA's Training Provider Registry
choice_c: Obtain a letter from their employer only
choice_d: Pass a written essay exam
explanation: The manual states that to be eligible to take the Class A or Class B CDL skills test, the S or P skills test, or the H knowledge test, applicants must have completed applicable entry-level driver training from a registered training provider listed on FMCSA's Training Provider Registry.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, ELDT Entry-Level Driver Training

question: What is the maximum validity period of a Medical Examiner's Certificate for a Hawaii CDL holder?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: A maximum of two years
choice_c: Five years
choice_d: It never expires once issued
explanation: The manual states a Medical Certificate is valid for a maximum of two years, and to maintain CDL status the Medical Examiner's Certificate must be kept current.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Medical and Physical Requirements

question: What happens if a driver who is required to have a 'certified' medical status fails to provide and keep up-to-date their medical examiner's certificate?
choice_a: Nothing changes as long as they self-certify verbally
choice_b: They become 'not-certified' and may lose their CDL
choice_c: They automatically receive a V restriction with no other consequence
choice_d: Their CLP is extended by 180 days
explanation: The manual warns that if a driver required to have a certified medical status fails to provide and keep up-to-date their medical examiner's certificate, they become 'not-certified' and may lose their CDL.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Medical Documentation Requirements

question: How old must a person be to be eligible for a Hawaii CDL, according to the manual?
choice_a: 18 years old
choice_b: 21 years old
choice_c: 25 years old
choice_d: 16 years old
explanation: The manual states you must be 21 years old to be eligible for a CDL.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Age Requirement

question: What fee must a Hawaii CDL applicant pay in advance to schedule an appointment for the skills test?
explanation: The manual lists a $50 fee paid in advance to schedule an appointment to take the skills tests; only applicants with prepaid appointments and proof of payment are allowed to test.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, What Fees Do I Pay?

question: What is the required order of the three parts of Hawaii's CDL practical (skills) test, and what happens if one part is failed?
choice_a: On-road driving, basic control, pre-trip inspection; only the failed part must be retaken
choice_b: Pre-trip Inspection, Basic Control Skills Test, and On-road Driving Test, in that order; if any part is failed, the whole test is failed and must be rescheduled
choice_c: Basic control, pre-trip inspection, on-road driving; failing one part has no effect on the others
choice_d: The order is chosen randomly by the examiner each time
explanation: The manual states the order of the tests is Pre-trip Inspection, Basic Control Skills Test, and On-road Driving Test, and that if any part is failed, the whole test is failed and the whole test must be rescheduled.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Special Instructions for Skills Testing

question: What happens if an applicant fails the Air Brake test during the skills test appointment?
choice_a: It has no effect on the rest of the test
choice_b: It is an automatic failure for the Pre-Trip Inspection test, and the test is discontinued at that point
choice_c: The applicant is given a second attempt immediately
choice_d: Only the On-road Driving Test is affected
explanation: The manual specifies that failure of the Air Brake test is an automatic failure for the Pre-Trip Inspection test, and the test will be discontinued at that point.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Special Instructions for Skills Testing

question: What is the maximum time allowed for the entire practical test if a Class A vehicle is used, compared to a Class B or lower vehicle?
choice_a: One hour for Class A; 30 minutes for Class B or lower
choice_b: Two hours for Class A; one and one-half hours for Class B or lower
choice_c: Both are limited to one hour
choice_d: There is no time limit for either class
explanation: The manual states that one and one-half hours is the maximum time allowed for the entire practical test using a Class B or lower vehicle, and if a Class A vehicle is used, the maximum time is two hours.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Special Instructions for Skills Testing

question: Which knowledge test must be taken by every CDL applicant, regardless of vehicle class or endorsement?
choice_a: The air brakes test
choice_b: The general knowledge test
choice_c: The hazardous materials test
choice_d: The combination vehicles test
explanation: The manual states the general knowledge test is taken by all applicants, while other knowledge tests (air brakes, combination vehicles, hazmat, tank vehicle, doubles/triples, school bus) apply only to specific vehicle types or endorsements.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Commercial Driver License Tests

question: How does Hawaii administer CDL knowledge and skills testing?
choice_a: Testing is administered by four County Commercial Driver Licensing Offices (Honolulu, Hawaii, Maui, and Kauai) using one shared statewide manual
choice_b: Testing is administered entirely online with no in-person component
choice_c: Only the City and County of Honolulu offers CDL testing statewide
choice_d: Each county publishes its own separate CDL manual with different content
explanation: The manual lists Commercial Driver Licensing Offices for the City and County of Honolulu, County of Hawaii, County of Maui, and County of Kauai, all operating under this single statewide CDL manual, similar to how Hawaii's regular driver licensing is administered by county.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Commercial Driver Licensing Offices

question: Under Hawaii's major offense rules (HRS 286-240), what is the general suspension period for a first offense such as driving a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.04% or more?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: One year
choice_c: Five years
choice_d: Lifetime
explanation: The manual states that major offenses under HRS 286-240, including driving a CMV with a BAC of 0.04% or more, generally carry a one-year suspension for a first offense.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, What Happens if I Am Convicted of a CDL Disqualifying Offense?

question: Which major offense results in a lifetime disqualification even on a first offense, according to the manual?
choice_a: Following the vehicle ahead too closely
choice_b: Using a motor vehicle in the commission of a felony involving manufacturing, distributing, or dispensing a controlled substance
choice_c: Speeding 10 mph over the posted limit
choice_d: Failing to renew a CLP within 180 days
explanation: The manual specifically marks the use of a motor vehicle in the commission of a felony involving manufacturing, distributing, or dispensing a controlled substance (and severe trafficking in persons) as carrying a lifetime disqualification.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Major Offenses

question: What speed threshold qualifies as 'excessive speeding' under Hawaii's serious traffic violation rules (HRS 286-231)?
choice_a: Any speed 5 mph or more above the posted limit
choice_b: Any speed 15 mph or more above the posted speed limit
choice_c: Any speed over 65 mph regardless of posted limit
choice_d: Any speed 25 mph or more above the posted limit
explanation: The manual defines excessive speeding as a serious traffic violation involving any speed of 15 mph or more above the posted speed limit.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Serious Traffic Violations

question: A CMV driver in Hawaii who violates a state or local law prohibiting texting while driving a CMV has committed what kind of violation?
choice_a: A minor parking infraction with no CDL impact
choice_b: A serious traffic violation under HRS 286-231
choice_c: An imminent hazard disqualification only
choice_d: A railroad-highway grade crossing offense
explanation: The manual lists violating a state or local law or ordinance prohibiting texting while driving a CMV as one of the enumerated serious traffic violations under HRS 286-231.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Serious Traffic Violations

question: The manual states that a driver may not hold more than one license. What happens if a driver breaks this rule?
choice_a: Nothing, as long as the licenses are from different states
choice_b: A court may fine the driver up to $5,000 or put them in jail, and keep their home state license while returning any others
choice_c: The driver simply pays a $50 fee
choice_d: The driver's medical certificate is automatically revoked
explanation: The manual states you cannot have more than one license; if you break this rule, a court may fine you up to $5,000 or put you in jail, keep your home state license, and return any others.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Other CDL Rules

question: Why must CDL holders be properly restrained by a safety belt at all times while operating a CMV, according to the manual?
choice_a: Because it is only a suggestion, not a rule
choice_b: Because unbelted drivers are four times more likely to be fatally injured if thrown from the vehicle, and the belt helps the driver control the vehicle during a crash
choice_c: Because it is required only for drivers under age 25
choice_d: Because it prevents speeding tickets
explanation: The manual explains that the safety belt holds the driver securely behind the wheel during a crash, helping control the vehicle and reducing serious injury or death; if you do not wear a safety belt, you are four times more likely to be fatally injured if thrown from the vehicle.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Other CDL Rules

question: What is a CDL holder prohibited from doing regarding mobile telephones while driving, per the manual?
choice_a: Nothing; mobile phone use is unrestricted
choice_b: Holding a mobile telephone to conduct a voice communication, or dialing by pressing more than a single button, and sending or reading text messages while driving
choice_c: Only hands-free calling is prohibited
choice_d: Using a phone is allowed as long as the vehicle is stopped at a light
explanation: The manual states CDL holders are not allowed to hold a mobile telephone to conduct a voice communication or dial by pressing more than a single button, and are not allowed to send or read text messages while driving.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 1 - Introduction, Other CDL Rules
